newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-HAWERCHUK HAT TRICK LEADS FLYERS PAST PENGUINS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-HAWERCHUK HAT TRICK LEADS FLYERS PAST PENGUINS.

text.p: Dale Hawerchuk recorded his 14th career hat trick and first in more than four years as the Philadelphia Flyers kept the Pittsburgh Penguins winless on the road with a 7-3 romp Thursday.
Hawerchuk had three goals and an assist as the Flyers found the net a season-high seven times. It was his first hat trick since February 1992 as a member of the Buffalo Sabres.

"It's always fun to get, but the big thing was our hockey club got going offensively and I thought we played a pretty solid game defensively, especially against a team with offensive weapons like that," said Hawerchuk.
Trent Klatt, Rod Brind'Amour and John LeClair each added a goal and an assist for Philadelphia, which won for just the second time in its last seven home games (2-4-1).
Jaromir Jagr scored his league-leading 16th goal for the Penguins, who fell to 0-11-1 on the road. The longest road winless streak in team history is 18 games, set in 1970-71 and equalled in 1982-83.
"It's starting to get kind of tough," conceded Pittsburgh centre Petr Nedved.
The crowd of 19,515 was the largest to view a hockey game in Pennsylvania history.

In St Louis, Harry York set up Brett Hull's tying goal with seven seconds left in regulation, then scored the game-winner 57 seconds into overtime as the Blues rallied past the Phoenix Coyotes 4-3 for their sixth win in seven games.
Hull was left alone at the bottom of the left faceoff circle and flicked a shot under goalie Nikolai Khabibulin's right arm for the tying tally.
"I was shooting for that (short) side, but I'm not going to tell you that's exactly where I was aiming," Hull said.

York won it with his second goal of the game. He tried to deflect Hull's shot from the right circle, but Khabibulin got his right pad on the puck. York made two swipes at the rebound, finally backhanding the puck from the top of the crease for his eighth of the season.
"It's the feeling of a lifetime," York said.
"Anytime a team scores with 6.3 seconds remaining, I classify that as deflating," said Coyotes assistant coach Paul MacLean.
In Boston, Mark Recchi recorded his second career hat trick and linemate Saku Koivu added a goal and two assists as the Montreal Canadiens routed the Bruins 6-2.
Jocelyn Thibault made 35 saves for the Canadiens, who improved to 2-9-1 on the road.

Recchi, who had just one goal in his previous eight games, tallied twice in the second period to extend Montreal's lead to 4-0. He completed his first hat trick since 1991, when he scored with 9:44 left in the third.
Bill Ranford surrendered six goals on 31 shots and was replaced by Scott Bailey.

In Edmonton, Andrei Kovalenko's goal during a two-man advantage broke a second-period tie and Curtis Joseph made 23 saves as the Oilers held on for a 3-2 victory over the floundering New York Rangers.
Edmonton won for just the third time in its last 10 games (3-6-1).
Brian Leetch set up both goals for New York, winless in seven of its last eight games (1-6-1).
The return of former Oilers Mark Messier and Wayne Gretzky as teammates drew the second sellout crowd of the season at the Edmonton Coliseum.

In San Jose, Nicklas Lidstrom scored a pair of power-play goals in a 52-second span in the first period and Steve Yzerman moved into second place on Detroit's all-time scoring list as the Red Wings cruised to a 6-1 victory over the punchless Sharks.

Yzerman had a goal and two assists, giving him 1,282 points to pass Alex Delvecchio into second place behind Gordie Howe on the all-time list. Yzerman did it in 964 games while Delvecchio needed 1,549.
The Sharks are winless in their last five games (0-4-1) and have scored just 13 goals in their last seven contests.

In Buffalo, Matthew Barnaby had two goals and two assists and Derek Plante added a pair of goals as the Sabres scored three straight in the third period for a 6-3 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs and a split of their home-and-home series.
Wendel Clark had a goal and an assist for the Maple Leafs, who have lost six straight road games. Toronto has dropped five of its last six, overall.
In Vancouver, Chris Joseph scored a power-play goal with 69 seconds left in overtime to give the Canucks a 2-1 victory over the Chicago Blackhawks.

The Canucks killed off Scott Walker's elbowing penalty in overtime, before Esa Tikkanen stole the puck from defenceman Keith Carney behind the Chicago net. He held the puck, then passed to Joseph, who streaked down the left wing before ripping a slap shot over goaltender Jeff Hackett's glove.
Tony Amonte scored in the first period for Chicago and Pavel Bure tied it up at 13:56 of the third.
